decks.notes: This deck aims to disrupt the opponent's game plan by playing hate cards like Archon of Emeria and Chancellor of the Annex, while also putting pressure on the opponent with aggressive creatures like White Plume Adventurer and Witch Enchanter. The deck also utilizes powerful artifacts like Black Lotus and Moxen to accelerate its mana production. By combining aggressive creatures with disruptive elements, this deck seeks to control the game and hinder the opponent's ability to execute their strategy effectively.

The main idea of this deck is to aggressively use Bazaar of Baghdad to fill the graveyard with powerful creatures like Hollow One, Vengevine, and Squee, Goblin Nabob. By utilizing free spells like Force of Will and Force of Negation, as well as disruptive cards like Wasteland and Chalice of the Void, the deck can disrupt the opponent while quickly overwhelming them with a swarm of creatures. The deck also includes card draw and graveyard recursion effects to maintain momentum and consistency in executing its game plan.

The deck focuses on using efficient counterspells and removal spells to control the game, while also utilizing card draw and selection to maintain card advantage and find key pieces. It includes powerful mana acceleration and card advantage cards such as Ancestral Recall, Black Lotus, and Demonic Tutor. The inclusion of Lurrus of the Dream-Den as a companion allows for additional value by recurring small creatures. The deck's win condition is through incremental advantage and controlling the game until eventually overwhelming the opponent with threats or grinding them out of resources.

This Dimir Control deck focuses on efficient card advantage, disruption, and controlling the board through counterspells and removal. It utilizes Orrish Bowmasters and Psychic Frogs to control the opponent's creatures while also disrupting their hand with cards like Gitaxian Probe and Thoughtseize. The deck also aims to manipulate the graveyard with cards like Dig Through Time and Treasure Cruise for additional value. The inclusion of companion Lurrus of the Dream-Den adds a versatile threat to the deck, allowing for additional recursion and value over a longer game.

The deck focuses on utilizing powerful disruption spells and card draw to control the board while deploying efficient threats to pressure the opponent. By combining aggressive creatures like Orcish Bowmasters and Deathrite Shaman with disruptive spells like Force of Will and Fatal Push, the deck aims to disrupt the opponent's game plan while steadily building up its own resources. The inclusion of Lurrus of the Dream-Den as a companion provides additional value and resilience in longer games. Overall, the deck seeks to outmaneuver opponents with a mix of aggression and disruption in a midrange shell.

This Vintage 1 vs 1 deck focuses on using the Coveted Jewel card to generate massive card advantage and mana acceleration. The deck includes powerful artifacts like The One Ring, Mana Crypt, and Grim Monolith to ramp up quickly and control the game with counterspells like Force of Will. The combo potential is high with cards like Tinker and Time Vault, while additional utility is provided by cards like Karn, the Great Creator and Mystic Forge. With strong mana sources like Mishra's Workshop and Tolarian Academy, this deck aims to overwhelm the opponent with its powerful artifacts and efficient plays.

This deck focuses on using control elements to disrupt the opponent's strategy while steadily building card advantage and mana advantage. The inclusion of Lurrus of the Dream-Den as a companion adds an extra dimension to the deck by allowing the player to consistently recur low-cost permanents. The deck includes a mix of counterspells, removal, and card draw to control the game and outvalue the opponent. The strategy is to maintain control of the board and resources until victory can be secured through incremental advantage.

With efficient mana acceleration from Moxen and lands like Ancient Tomb and Cavern of Souls, along with disruptive elements like Chalice of the Void and Mental Misstep, the deck aims to establish an aggressive board presence early on and disrupt the opponent's game plan to secure a swift victory.

The main idea of this deck is to aggressively disrupt and slow down the opponent while quickly building up a board presence with hatebears. It aims to control the game through cards like Archon of Emeria and Chancellor of the Annex, while utilizing disruptive lands like Wasteland and Karakas. The deck also includes efficient mana acceleration with Moxen and can generate card advantage with Seasoned Dungeoneer and Witch Enchanter. Additionally, it can protect its key cards with cards like Anointed Peacekeeper and Solitude, making it a versatile and powerful aggro-hatebear deck in Vintage 1 vs 1 format.

This deck focuses on using the card Doomsday to set up a powerful win condition by manipulating the top cards of the library. It includes fast mana accelerants like Mox Jet and Black Lotus, as well as a range of card draw and manipulation spells to find and set up the Doomsday combo. The deck also includes protection spells like Force of Will and Flusterstorm to ensure the combo is successful. The goal is to efficiently assemble the right combination of cards to win the game in a single turn.

The focus of this deck is overwhelming the opponent with aggressive artifact creatures, backed up by disruptive cards like Null Rod, Sphere of Resistance, and Thorn of Amethyst. The deck also aims to lock down the opponent's resources with cards like Wasteland and Crucible of Worlds while generating advantage with Golos, Tireless Pilgrim and Stonecoil Serpent. Karn, the Great Creator provides utility and additional threats, making it difficult for the opponent to mount a defense. Overall, the deck seeks to establish early dominance and maintain pressure throughout the game.
